questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. That it was a French speaking country as i really want to be more fluent in the language. 
2. That it was located in EU: partially due to corona (it was easier to get home and in general to travel back and forth) but also because I wanted to have friends and family from Denmark visiting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the administration in France is really bad and a therefore a bit stressfull - which is why i only gave it 9 starts.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy at all! I tried 6 months before i came to check everything and get everything fixed. But i ended up having none of the courses i wanted and when i asked my Erasmus coordinater at my home university, she was not even sure what kind of courses i was allowed to take.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I got a welcome bag with very nice stuff! and i really appreciate that. But everything else i had to figure out. 
I came to Paris 3 weeks before the courses started because i couldn't find informations anywhere! and the courses i had found in advance started the first week of Jan. Since i didn't get an answer regardin which courses i was allowed to i didn't get information regarding where any of the lectures took place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The administration is not so good in France

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I asked around in a group called padam padam. And then i knew someone who knew someone.. not very difficult to find housing. i was also offered to stay at a student residence which Sorbonne helped me with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would actually not recommend to live off campus. If i go to france again i would like to apply for Cite universitaire as it is a very great place for students to live. You are amongst a lot of other students and there are a great and cheap canteen and a lot of different events and sport-possibilities as well as good transport connection.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration was the easy part. finding which courses i was allowed to take was the most difficult part! I even asked some people from Paris before i went on exchange, and they also have a hard time finding out which courses are available. And further, almost all the courses are in french - which i didn't know. but it is important that it says before a student enroll, because if the student knows it, there are a lot of good courses avaliable.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: i had to write to my Erasmus coordinator - who did not always reply. sometimes 2 months past!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: only the Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not Successfull - i didn't get any of the courses i wanted and I only got 12 ECTS out of 30 which was relevant for my education.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware, that you will need to take courses in French if you are a master student on the 1 st year or under. else the courses are very very limited (or almost non-exsisting)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I know there are some great courses at Sorbonne, but they are in French. I didn't know beforehand which is why i have had set my mind up to receive courses in English. If i had known, i would still had applied, but i would be much more prepaired.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In France, the master is devided into 2 parts (M1 and M2). The M1 is a bit under the level in Denmark (at least at the university i took courses (paris physics master)). for me it was good, as i didn't study physics at my bachelor. Other students might find it too easy. Maybe the courses at Sorbonne is a bit more advanced (but they are in French).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of the teachers were very good and especially my supervisors in my internship! It's the same style as in Denmark - you have a lecture - then you have some reading material and then you have some exercises.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advanced Quantum Mechanics 2 (3 ECTS), Atomic and molecular physics (6 ECTS), Localized spins in solids (3ECTS), French course (3ECTS), Condensed matter physics (6ECTS), Internship (9ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: almost all the masters in France have an internship in the 2. semester - so that is mandatory if your home University requires at least 30 ECTS. then i would recommend Advanced quantum mechanics 2 as the teacher was fantastic - you learn about group theory and the dirac equation. Condensed matter physics was also okay, but it does not really cover magnetism which i would have loved.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it cost money to get a bank account - there are a lot of banks - some of them even give you money to be in the bank. However, transfering all your money to your french bank account is around 350 dkk. I would recommend you to use Revolut or something similar.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The food is less expensive in restaurants in France compared to denmark. 
Buying food in the supermarkets are more expensive than buying food in the streetmarkets. 
There is a canteen for students called (Crous) - it's located all around Paris - where you get 3 courses for 3.3 Euro. It's much less than if you should make your own food.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You need a "lægeerklæring" in order to do sports.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds! - Badminton, yoga, swimming etc. and also language course is free at Sorbonne if you are a student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: sport-activities in order to get native french-speaking friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities than Paris - Normandie (étretat), fontainebleau etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: go to sport activities! there are only french people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Many french people (even young people) do not speak french!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the beautiful architecture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take all the courses in French. - the courses in english are not so good.
Apply for the facebook group Padam Padam.
Go to the website
https://frederikskirkenparis.dk/
- you will find a lot of usefull information there regarding living in Paris.
Apply for the Cite universitaire - it's a beautifull place to live and you are surrounded by a lot of other young people.
Get a french number! you actually cannot make accounts many places without a french number. I just bought a "taletidskort" for 5 euros.
Travel with Parismus!
Eat a lot of cheese!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You can be very good at French without people understand what you are saying. French people are a bit picky with how you pronounce the things. 
The administration is not so good, but hang in! you will figure it out in the end even though it takes many many hours!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get a lot of new friends from all around the world. To be able to listen to french and understand very well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
